correctness.rationale: Direct substitution gives the positive fixed point. Euclidean-normalization differentiation yields an exactly graph-diagonal Jacobian. All radial and tangential multipliers are determined by one positive-denominator formula; sign analysis of a concave step quadratic proves the sharp stable, neutral, and unstable regions, including the factorization at zero killing. Packaged VERIFY.py independently replays exact symbolic checks, an exact-rational path example and finite-difference tests (1208 assertions). The analytic proof, not finite checks, handles all finite connected graphs. The neutral nonlinear boundary is intentionally unproved.

value.rationale: The homogeneous defocusing graph Gross–Pitaevskii problem is a natural numerical-optimization test bed. The exact critical step, its transition from top-frequency crossing under uniform leakage to simultaneous graph-independent crossing at zero leakage, and explicit unstable example diagnose parameter selection beyond the earlier sufficient small-step theory. The result is substantive locally even without global convergence or a complete nonlinear flip bifurcation.
